User has selected the official Espressif ESP32-S31 Korvo factory_demo as the final performance/platform demo, implemented USING OPENVELA, not by flashing ESP-IDF. Preserve the separate digit-recognition demo. Prior field-registration demo is superseded. Shared workspace /home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela. Official pinned source is being downloaded (main/UI already present) into backups/factory-demo-port/upstream/examples/esp32-s31-korvo/examples/factory_demo, commit recorded in upstream-commit.json. Current E402 SMP native services + WiFi + BLE + MEDIA build is still running: DO NOT change maintained sources or build inputs, do not start full builds, do not access serial/USB/boards. Write only inside YOUR private directory under backups/factory-demo-port. Use actual openvela APIs, preserve upstream notices/licenses, no mocked hardware success or invented performance. Do not spawn other workers. Source modifications stay private; root integrates after review. Need concrete code/candidate and concise result, not just advice. Keep required original factory capabilities in scope. Read local relevant instructions. English source/comments/public docs. Existing root s31-reference AGENTS restriction against UI is overridden by explicit user scope. Current LVGL is 9.x, upstream UI is 9.2.2. Existing native application example: openvela-dev/frameworks/runtimes/services/xmsdemo/platform and lvgldemo; framework uikit/window LVGL APIs. Build compile_commands reference is backups/product-integration-execution/build-v1/build/compile_commands.json. No full firmware build; small targeted compile checks are allowed after candidate prepared.

YOUR DIRECTORY: /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/peripherals-port

Own real openvela hardware backend for the factory dashboard. Inspect upstream main/main.c and factory_demo_audio/camera/usb_hid, and existing maintained Korvo openvela drivers/apps. Create private FactoryBackend.h/.cpp or C module with safe asynchronous snapshots and start/stop/capture/record/play/SD-probe/buttons/LED/HID support using actual openvela interfaces. Prefer current MEDIA for audio and driver devices for camera/input, preserve full source scope; identify genuinely missing driver API rather than faking. Propose backend contract in contracts.md early so root/UI worker can align. Camera must expose RGB565 frames for LVGL canvas without owning/reinitializing the framebuffer; find current camera-only capture ioctl interfaces vs preview driver and add narrowly scoped private driver changes only if needed. Use bounded buffers, pthread mutexes, cancel/cleanup ownership, no LVGL calls from worker. SD read/write verifies a unique own test file, do not touch user data; HID should read existing native mouse/keyboard nodes. Physical hearing deferred until speaker present, show actual completion not hearing claim. Include profile prerequisites and exact device/API facts. No full build/hardware. Concrete candidate files, targeted compile checks if possible, result.md.

I’ll inspect the local instructions and the pinned upstream/backend APIs first, then draft the backend contract and implement the private hardware module under `peripherals-port`. I’ll keep changes isolated there, avoid firmware builds and board access, and finish with targeted static/compile checks plus `result.md`.

The MEDIA API already provides callback-based playback completion and recorder lifecycle control. I’m defining the UI boundary around copied snapshots and copied RGB565 frames so worker threads never touch LVGL. The important remaining check is which Korvo camera node can capture without taking over `/dev/fb0`.

The existing `/dev/video0` V4L2 bridge can supply RGB565 without opening the framebuffer, so no camera-driver patch is needed for that boundary. I’ve written `contracts.md` with two integration limits: E402 currently disables several factory devices, and its MEDIA graph has playback only. Also, the UI draft’s 500 ms shutdown promise is incompatible with the current MEDIA control/stop timeouts; cleanup must retain ownership until worker joins complete.

The private backend now has separate camera, audio, and peripheral workers. It uses native V4L2 capture, MEDIA-owned cancellable PCM I/O, verified SD probe files, ADC button state, WS2812 writes, and native HID reads. I’m checking compile compatibility and the failure paths next—especially frame leases, MEDIA callback lifetime, and device teardown.

The first target syntax check passed. The deeper review found a genuine USB mouse gap: the current mouse upper half frees its state on unregister while an application may still hold an open descriptor. I’m keeping the native mouse reader in the candidate but disabling it by default until that hot-unplug lifetime issue is fixed; keyboard monitoring can use the existing native API. The review also confirmed that SD and USB host, like camera and keys, are currently excluded from SMP by Kconfig.

Both the backend with all implementation paths enabled and the private camera ownership patch compile with the target compiler. The patch only rejects a second independent opener of the deferred-copy camera queue, so one application cannot retain another application’s capture buffers after close. I’m finalizing the handoff with the required profile changes and the remaining shutdown and mouse-driver blockers clearly separated from compile results.

The handoff report is complete, including exact device paths, memory bounds, native API prerequisites, and source evidence for the blockers. The backend and camera patch have passed targeted RISC-V compile checks; I’m saving the final receipts and file hashes. No hardware or firmware build was used for validation.

Created the private [backend candidate](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/peripherals-port/candidate/FactoryBackend.cpp), [contract](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/peripherals-port/contracts.md), and [result report](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/peripherals-port/result.md).

Target compile checks passed, including all backend paths and the narrow camera ownership patch.

Integration blockers are documented: SMP profile exclusions, missing MEDIA capture components, unsafe mouse hot-unplug lifetime, and the impossible 500 ms shutdown guarantee. Mouse opening remains disabled pending its driver fix.

No maintained sources, full builds, boards, or digit-demo files were touched.
